turns.t: Hi. Mum said I had to come on my own, because she's at work and I'm fifteen. I've got chickenpox. At least I think so.
That's fine, I'll make sure we talk through everything. When did the spots start?
Three days ago. Now they're all over, but nothing in my mouth.
Any fever or feeling unwell?
Yeah, I had a temperature the first day, and a headache. Not now.
And what's been done about it so far? Let me go through what you're using.

Calamine lotion, on the spots. Paracetamol, 500 mg, when I'm hot, maybe three a day. Cetirizine, 10 mg at night, so I can sleep. My inhaler, the blue one, when I wheeze. And emollient cream, for my eczema, twice a day.
That's a lot, and it sounds sensible. Any conditions apart from the chickenpox?
Asthma, and eczema.
Any operations?
Just my tonsils, when I was eight.
Do you do sport, or go out anywhere?
I play netball. But obviously not now.
Do you have any allergies to medicines?
No. None that I know of.
Good. Let me look at your spots. ~
They're everywhere.
There are red spots and blisters in different stages, some scabbed, over your chest, back and arms, and none look infected.
Is it definitely chickenpox? ~
Yes, the pattern is typical.
Oh good. Am I contagious? ~
Until every spot has scabbed over, usually about five days after the spots began, so stay home.
When can I go back to school? ~
When all the spots have crusted over. Don't go near anyone who's pregnant, or has a weak immune system, or a newborn. ~
My auntie is pregnant. ~
Keep away from her until you're better.
Right. ~
Keep taking the paracetamol, but avoid ibuprofen, it can make chickenpox skin infections worse, and with asthma, it's best avoided.
Okay. ~
And keep your nails short. Try not to scratch. ~
It's so itchy though. ~
The cetirizine and the calamine are the right things. Cool baths help too. ~
Will they scar? ~
If you don't scratch, most don't. ~
Okay. ~
Come back if the spots become red, swollen and sore, you get a high fever, breathing problems, or you can't keep fluids down.
I will. Thanks. ~
